'''''Leonotis''''' is a [[genus]] of [[flowering plant]]s in the [[Family (taxonomy)|family]] [[Lamiaceae]].<ref name="harley2004">Raymond M. Harley, Sandy Atkins, Andrey L. Budantsev, Philip D. Cantino, Barry J. Conn, Renée J. Grayer, Madeline M. Harley, Rogier P.J. de Kok, Tatyana V. Krestovskaja, Ramón Morales, Alan J. Paton, and P. Olof Ryding. 2004. "Labiatae" pages 167-275. In: Klaus Kubitzki (editor) and Joachim W. Kadereit (volume editor). ''The Families and Genera of Vascular Plants'' volume VII. Springer-Verlag: Berlin; Heidelberg, Germany. {{ISBN|978-3-540-40593-1}}</ref> One species, ''[[Leonotis nepetifolia]]'', is [[Indigenous (ecology)|native]] to [[tropical Africa]] and [[southern India]]. It is [[Naturalisation (biology)|naturalized]] throughout most of the [[tropics]]. The other species are [[Endemism|endemic]] to southern and eastern [[Africa]].<ref name=a>[http://apps.kew.org/wcsp/namedetail.do?name_id=109426 Kew World Checklist of Selected Plant Families]</ref><ref name="iwarsson2003">Mattias Iwarsson and Yvette Harvey. 2003. "Monograph of the genus ''Leonotis'' (Pers.) R.Br. (Lamiaceae)". ''Kew Bulletin'' '''58'''(3):597-645.</ref>

''Leonotis'' was named by [[Robert Brown (Scottish botanist from Montrose)|Robert Brown]] in 1810 in [[Prodromus Florae Novae Hollandiae et Insulae Van Diemen]].<ref name="brown1810">Robert Brown. 1810. ''Prodromus Florae Novae Hollandiae et Insulae Van Diemen'':504. (see ''External links'' below).</ref> The name means "lion's ear".

The [[Type (biology)|type]] for the genus is the [[Biological specimen|specimen]] of ''[[Leonotis ocymifolia]]'' that was originally described as ''Leonotis leonitis''.<ref name="ingleonotis">''Leonotis'' In: Index Nominum Genericorum. In: [[Regnum Vegetabile]] (see ''External links'' below).</ref> It is a specimen of ''Leonotis ocymifolia var. ocymifolia''.<ref name="iwarsson2003"/>

This plant genus is reportedly [[Psychoactive drug|psychoactive]] and [[sedating]], with a "high" similar to a that of a small dose of [[hashish]]. {{cn|date=June 2026}}

==Taxonomy==
''Leonotis'' is a member of the [[subfamily]] [[Lamioideae]].<ref name="harley2004"/> ''Leonotis'' might be [[paraphyletic]] or even [[polyphyletic]] because ''[[Leonotis leonurus]]'' is not closely related to the other species.<ref name="scheen2009">Anne-Cathrine Scheen and Victor A. Albert. 2009. "Molecular Phylogenetics of the ''Leucas'' Group (Lamioideae; Lamiaceae)". ''Systematic Botany'' '''34'''(1):173-181.</ref> In 2009, it was shown that ''Leonotis'' and 3 other genera are [[Paraphyly|embedded]] in ''[[Leucas]]'',<ref name="scheen2009"/> a genus of about 100 species.<ref name="harley2004"/> If the 4 embedded genera were merged with ''Leucas'', the expanded ''Leucas'' would have about 132 species.
